Invoices

spezado writes invoices as XRechnung 3.0 – an XML file after EN 16931 – or as ZUGFeRD – a PDF to read with the same XRechnung attached for machines (profile XRECHNUNG). Since 2025 businesses in Germany must be able to receive e-invoices (BMF); both formats are e-invoices. The file written is the original: it is kept with the invoice and can be downloaded again.

Before the first invoice

  • The seller – your name, address, contact with phone and e-mail, VAT identification number and/or tax number, the IBAN to pay to, the days until payment is due and the prefix of the numbers (terminal: p on Documents).
  • A customer – name, address, the e-mail invoices go to, the VAT identification number for supplies to businesses abroad or under reverse charge, and the reference a public authority asked for (its Leitweg-ID) (terminal: k).

Writing one

An invoice has a customer, a date, the day of the supply, lines – what, how much, the unit (hours, days, pieces), the net price and a tax code –, a note and the file to write. Numbers follow in sequence per year: RE-2026-001, RE-2026-002, … On a cash basis the invoice is booked when it is paid – the bank proposes it for the entry that pays it –; with double entry the receivable is booked when the invoice is issued.

Tax code Category (EN 16931) What the invoice states
de-out-19, de-out-7 S – 19 % or 7 %  
de-out-0 Z – 0 % (§ 12 Abs. 3 UStG)  
de-out-exempt E – exempt (§ 4 UStG) the reason you give – „Steuerfrei nach § 4 Nr. 14 UStG.“ –, a general one otherwise
de-out-13b AE – reverse charge at home (§ 13b UStG) „Steuerschuldnerschaft des Leistungsempfängers“
de-out-eu-service AE – a service to a business in another EU country (§ 3a Abs. 2 UStG) „Steuerschuldnerschaft des Leistungsempfängers“
de-out-ig-supply K – intra-Community supply „Steuerfreie innergemeinschaftliche Lieferung“
de-out-export G – export „Steuerfreie Ausfuhrlieferung“
none – small business E – § 19 UStG „Gemäß § 19 UStG wird keine Umsatzsteuer berechnet.“

The statements are those § 14 Abs. 4 Nr. 8 and § 14a UStG ask for (§ 14a UStG). spezado checks before writing what they need: a customer in Germany for § 13b, a customer in another country for EU services and intra-Community supplies, and the VAT identification numbers of both sides where they must be on the invoice.

XRechnung and ZUGFeRD

Both carry the same data and are checked against the rules of XRechnung before they are written.

  • XRechnung (RE-2026-001.xml, UBL): XML only, as the German public administration receives invoices (XRechnung).
  • ZUGFeRD (RE-2026-001.pdf) is a PDF/A-3b for people – set in Domitian, with the address in the window of a DIN 5008 envelope – with the XRechnung in CII attached as xrechnung.xml. ZUGFeRD invoices written by spezado pass veraPDF (PDF/A-3b) and the Mustang validator (PDF/A-3b, EN 16931 and XRechnung rules).

Without a VAT identification number the seller’s tax number is also its identifier (BT-29): EN 16931 requires one of BT-29, BT-30 or BT-31 (rule BR-CO-26).

The seller’s details and the customers are part of the books – the owner’s contact and invoicing settings, the customers as organisations – and travel with them to every device. Each device writes invoice numbers in a series of its own, so that two devices offline never write the same number: the first RE-2026-001, the next ones RE-2026-B001, RE-2026-C001 (librotenado 0008). Should two devices ever have taken the same series, the review list says so.
